title: Any action fails attempting to write to /var/lib/containers/
body:
### Issue Description

Attempting to run any command fails, since podman tries to write to `/var/lib/containers`, which is root-owned. Regular users cannot write into this path.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

```
> podman info --debug
Error: creating runtime static files directory "/var/lib/containers/storage/libpod": mkdir /var/lib/containers/storage: permission denied
```

### Describe the results you received

It fails writing into a system directory.

### Describe the results you expected

It should use the regular system directory.

### podman info output

```yaml
> podman info
Error: creating runtime static files directory "/var/lib/containers/storage/libpod": mkdir /var/lib/containers/storage: permission denied
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

This seems to be after an upgrade of podman (5.8.6-r0 -> 6.1.0-r0)

### Additional information

Additional information like issue happens only occasionally or issue happens with a particular architecture or on a particular setting

comments.body:
`/etc/containers/storage.conf` has:

    runroot = "/run/containers/storage"

Won't this break unless podman is running as root?

AFAIK, this is the default config shipped by containers-common.
Actually, deleting `/etc/containers/storage.conf` makes no difference, so perhaps this value is the build-in default too?
Previously reported at https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29630, which op accidentally closed and cannot re-open.
